subject: Recap: inference cost & pilot scope for Hexware — workload economics
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Cassandra Li <cassandra.li@hexware.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: inference cost & pilot scope for Hexware — workload economics

Cassandra — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call so we have aligned next steps and success criteria. I've kept this high-level; happy to expand any section.

Pain points you described
- Cost volatility on peak days: current per-1M-token spend fluctuates and makes forecasting hard.
- Many short-lived requests (chat + small completions) so batching is underutilized; current batching kills latency for real-time flows.
- KV/prefix cache not in use across most endpoints due to multi-tenant routing constraints.
- Procurement needs a predictable pilot SOW and an estimate of cost delta vs current infra.

Current stack (as you described)
- Self-hosted endpoints on GCP (K8s) fronted by a small autoscaling layer.
- Triton + custom autoscaler; dynamic batcher but limits set to preserve 200ms SLO.
- Mix of generation (chat) + embeddings (reranking) workloads; embeddings account for ~25% of token volume.

Success criteria you called out (we captured)
- p95 end-to-end latency for interactive flows <= 300ms.
- Unit cost reduction target: ~35–45% per 1M generated tokens vs your baseline.
- No more than 2% quality regression on your eval prompt set (we'll run A/B).
- Pilot needs to show stable burst handling (QPS spikes up to ~200) without >10% request tail errors.

What Redwood proposes for pilot (initial scope)
- 2-week workload pilot on Redwood Dedicated (isolated capacity) using an A100-equivalent baseline.
- We will: ingest a 48–72 hour anonymized workload sample, run cost/latency simulation with batching and prefix caching enabled, and surface a tuned config (batching thresholds, cache policies, quantization profile suggestions).
- Deliverables: pilot report (metrics), recommended production config, and SOW for a follow-on rollout.

Open items / asks from Hexware
1) A 48–72 hour anonymized request log (timestamps, prompt length, response length, route) — sample manifest attached.
2) Confirmation on quantization openness: you mentioned youre cautious; a staged eval (FP16 -> int8 -> 4-bit) is acceptable if quality is validated. Please confirm "int8 OK" or "4-bit OK".
3) Procurement contact + desired timeline (you mentioned decision by ~Mar 15).

Next steps
- If you approve, we'll send an SOW + NDA for the workload sample and provision a sandbox Dedicated queue for the pilot.
- Proposed dates: pilot window Mar 8–Mar 22 (flexible).
- I'll schedule a 30m checkpoint next Wed to review the manifest upload process.

Attachments: pilot_scope_template.pdf, call_recording_20260225.mp3, sample_manifest.csv (manifest shows expected columns and anonymization guidance).

If that looks right, please reply with: the procurement contact, whether int8/4-bit quantization evaluation is acceptable, and confirm the pilot window or suggest alternatives.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform
From: Cassandra Li <cassandra.li@hexware.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: inference cost & pilot scope for Hexware — workload economics

Rachel — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick data points to help with the manifest and sizing:
- Average request payload (prompt only): ~85 tokens; average response length ~120 tokens.
- 75% of requests are under 128 tokens.
- Peak sustained QPS observed during business hours: ~150–180; nightly low ~10–20.
- Embeddings traffic spikes after batch index jobs; embeddings are sensitive to throughput but not strict latency.

Quantization: we are open to int8 for inference as long as it passes a quality baseline. 4-bit is a maybe; procurement will require a side-by-side evaluation on a representative prompt set.

Procurement lead: Jordan Myers (jordan.myers@hexware.ai) — loop them in for SOW/PO. Decision target: mid-March (aim to have pilot contract by Mar 12–16).

We can share anonymized logs once a mutual NDA is in place. For now, I gave your team read-only S3 access to a placeholder bucket where we'll drop a sanitized 24–48h sample: s3://hexware-prod-uploads/hexware-samples/ (you should see a small test file there later today).

Let's lock the checkpoint next Wed at 10:30 PT. I'll expect a calendar invite.

— Cassandra
Cassandra Li
Head of ML Platform, Hexware Inc.
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Cassandra Li <cassandra.li@hexware.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@hexware.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: inference cost & pilot scope for Hexware — workload economics

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Cassandra — this is perfect. Confirming items and next steps on our side:

1) Quantization: noted — we'll run an int8 baseline for the pilot and include a 4-bit evaluation only if the int8 results meet your quality bar. We'll include clear regression metrics in the pilot report.

2) Procurement contact added (Jordan) — Jordan, welcome. We'll attach a short SOW and an NDA to the HubSpot deal (link below) and route the SOW via DocuSign once we have your confirmation on the pilot window.

3) Data/sample: we'll use the S3 placeholder you gave for the initial upload. Jonas, can you coordinate the ingestion scripts and give them the manifest format?

Action items assigned
- Rachel: send SOW + NDA + calendar invite for 10:30 PT checkpoint (today: 26 Feb) and proposed pilot dates Mar 8–22. (target: send by EOD)
- Jonas: share ingestion instructions + manifest template in the S3 bucket and coordinate test upload.
- Marissa: prep a rough cost delta estimate (per-1M-token) based on the averages Cassandra shared; we'll include baseline vs optimized (batching + cache) numbers in the SOW.

Links / attachments
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345 HW-2026-0051
- S3 placeholder: s3://hexware-prod-uploads/hexware-samples/ (read-only test file expected)
- DocuSign SOW (placeholder): https://docusign.com/link/to/sow/HW-2026-0051
- Attachments sent: pilot_scope_template.pdf, sample_manifest.csv (manifest contains columns: timestamp, request_id, prompt_len, response_len, route, anonymized_user_id).

I'll send the calendar invite and SOW + NDA by EOD. If any of the success criteria needs rewording for procurement, let me know and we'll align the SOW.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
